messages:
rachel: noticing slow memory climb on long streaming chats with tool loops attached — +1.8GB over ~45m on a single session. attaching heap and kv pager stats. anyone else seen a similar shape? :thinking:

alex: can you paste the pmap / kv resident snapshot? also which kernel selection was used for that run?

rachel: we were on kernel-group v3 (fused-attn) with batch heuristics 'adaptive-quick'. repro on staging with seq=12k, tool loop enabling external-tool calls every 400 tokens. pmap: 
```
7f2c0000 kvmapped 12G rss
... kv_pages: active=1.2M free=80k reclaimed=4k
```
heap delta shows steady retained pages in page-buckets tagged "session-prefix".

ravi: ran heap profile; looks like page objects never hit eviction path. excerpt from gomem trace: 
```
# allocs by stack
  312K  runtime.kv_page_pin+0x34
  298K  runtime.session_attach_prefix+0x7c
  290K  runtime.kv_page_mark_live+0x18
```
Also saw repeated page references from tool-loop codepath (tool_msgs -> system_prefixes).

maria: hypothesis: tool loop appends short-lived system messages which create lots of small prefix fragments that keep pages pinned because our eviction uses contiguous-run heuristics. once fragmentation exceeds threshold, our quick-evict heuristic skips compaction. Suggest adding compaction pass when fragmentation > 30% or when stream length > 8k.

alex: +1 to instrumentation. small repro script that spikes this locally: 
```
# repro.sh
python tools/repro_stream.py --model tiny --seq 12000 --tool-loop 400 --keep-ttl 0
```
if folks can run with `KV_DEBUG=1` and attach `pagemap_dump` that helps.

rachel: ran marias compaction locally with a hacky patch — forced compaction on rollover — memory stopped growing, drops ~1.6GB. patch link: `github.com/rw/infra/patches/compaction-hotfix` (WIP).

deploy-bot: canary deploy queued: redwood/runtime:v3.1-evict-compaction-hotfix -> canary-3 (2 nodes)

ops: will monitor canary. set alert for session-rss > 2GB delta in 30m.

ravi: follow-ups: add unit test to simulate many small prefix appends + tool loop; instrument kernel path where `kv_page_try_evict` returns EARLY_SKIP with reason codes. please add reason code to logs so we can correlate.

alex: I'll add the reason-code patch and small unit test. also want to try a middle-ground heuristic: prefer compaction over skipping when session length > threshold instead of absolute fragmentation percent.

rachel: thanks — if canary looks good we'll roll to staging. tagging @maria for perf review and @ops for SLA notes. :thumbsup:
